terms.why: Hollandaise and béarnaise are raw-egg sauces, and the benny yolk runs as well.
terms.makeItGreen: Ask for the eggs cooked firm and the hollandaise left off. Smashed avo or a hot grilled tomato fills the gap.

terms.why: A runny, poached or soft-boiled yolk can carry salmonella.
terms.makeItGreen: Ask for the yolk cooked firm and the same plate is a green light.

terms.why: House-made aioli, mayo and garlic sauce are usually built on raw egg.
terms.makeItGreen: Ask whether it comes from a jar or a commercial bottle, because that lot is pasteurised and fine.

terms.why: The traditional caesar dressing is raw egg, and the meat on top is usually cold cured.
terms.makeItGreen: Ask for a bottled dressing and hot grilled chicken, or pick a different salad.

terms.why: Refrigerated pâté, parfait and terrine are chilled meat spreads: listeria risk plus a big hit of vitamin A.
terms.makeItGreen: A shelf-stable jar pâté or a white bean dip is all clear. If the parfait here is the yoghurt and granola kind, that one is fine too.

terms.why: Raw or pink-in-the-middle meat carries a toxoplasmosis risk.
terms.makeItGreen: Ask for it well done with no pink left, and it is back on the menu.

terms.why: Raw seafood can carry listeria, and citrus does not cook it either.
terms.makeItGreen: Ask for a cooked-filling roll made fresh, or the same fish grilled hot.

terms.why: Cold-smoked fish is chilled and never actually cooked, which is exactly the setup listeria likes.
terms.makeItGreen: Canned salmon, or smoked fish cooked right through in a hot dish, is a green light.

terms.why: Raw oysters and pre-cooked cold prawns are ready-to-eat seafood, so listeria gets a look in.
terms.makeItGreen: Order them hot: oysters Kilpatrick, or garlic prawns straight from the pan.

terms.why: Cold cured meat can carry listeria, and slicing it fresh does not make it safer.
terms.makeItGreen: Crisped hot in a pan or baked onto a pizza until it sizzles, it is back on.

terms.why: Cold deli meat is a listeria risk until it is heated right through.
terms.makeItGreen: Steaming hot on a pizza or pressed in a toastie, deli meat is a green light.

terms.why: Soft cheese can carry listeria unless the dish is cooked and served hot.
terms.makeItGreen: Baked, grilled or bubbling through a hot dish, soft cheese is back on the menu.

terms.why: Soft serve comes out of a dispenser machine that is hard to clean, and listeria can live inside one.
terms.makeItGreen: A scoop from a tub, a choc top, or a frozen banana blitzed at home does the same job.

terms.why: Raw sprouts are a known listeria carrier, every kind of them.
terms.makeItGreen: Ask for them left out or cooked right through in the wok, and the dish is a green light.

terms.why: The tahini in it is raw sesame, which can carry salmonella and listeria.
terms.makeItGreen: A white bean or beetroot dip scoops just as well, with no raw sesame in it.

terms.why: Enoki mushrooms have a listeria history unless they are cooked right through.
terms.makeItGreen: Simmered in a hot soup or fried off properly in a stir fry, enoki is fine.

terms.why: The rough rind traps bacteria, so the NSW Food Authority benches rockmelon entirely for now.
terms.makeItGreen: Watermelon, berries or any fruit cut fresh at home is a happy stand-in.

terms.why: These desserts are set with raw egg.
terms.makeItGreen: Baked desserts are all clear, so pav, a crumble or a hot sticky date has your back.

terms.why: Fermented drinks carry a contamination risk plus a little residual alcohol.
terms.makeItGreen: Sparkling water with lime, or a bottled pasteurised juice, hits the same spot.

terms.why: There is no safe amount of alcohol in pregnancy, and an espresso martini is a double whammy.
terms.makeItGreen: Sparkling water, lime and frozen berries in the good glass, or a zero-alcohol mocktail.

terms.why: Heads up, flake is shark. High-mercury fish is one serve a fortnight, with no other fish that fortnight.
terms.makeItGreen: Ask for snapper, whiting or flathead instead: same batter, same chips, no mercury cap.

terms.why: Mercury rule for this one: a single serve a week, and no other fish that week.
terms.makeItGreen: Snapper, barra, salmon or tinned tuna comes with no weekly cap.

terms.why: Liver is a vitamin A heavyweight, so the cap is 50g a week.
terms.makeItGreen: Keep it to one small slice a week, cooked right through.

terms.why: Caffeine has a daily cap of 200mg from everything combined, which is about 1 to 2 espresso coffees.
terms.makeItGreen: Keep the whole day under 200mg, and decaf is a free hug after that.

terms.why: Cooked hot right through, and heat is exactly what makes deli meat fine.
Beer batter is fried hot, so the question here is the fish: ask whether it is flake, which is shark.
A parmy comes out of the oven hot, ham and all. Pub classic, back on the menu.
